## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # IVector interface
//
// The interface shared by every numeric vector in this vocabulary
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_vector): component-wise arithmetic,
// norms, a dot product, and a read-and-construct component surface. The
// implementing types are declared in `vectors.types.plato` (the intrinsic
// Number2/3/4/8 tier) and `vectors.types.plato` (Vector2D/3D, VectorN,
// Direction2D/3D); the interface-generic bodies derived from this interface live in
// `numeric-structures.library.plato`.

// The family of fixed-arity numeric vectors: component-wise arithmetic, norms,
// dot product, and component-wise extremes
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_space).
//
// IIndexable<Number> supplies the read half of the component surface (Count is
// the arity, At(i) the i-th component). FromComponents and Broadcast supply the
// construction half, which is what makes component-wise map, zip, and fold
// derivable generically in `numeric-structures.library.plato` — every lifted
// Number function (Abs, Floor, Pow, Lerp, ...) and every reduction
// (SumComponents, MinComponent, Magnitude) is written once against this pair
// rather than once per concrete type.
interface IVector
    inherits INumerical, IArithmetic, IIndexable<Number>, INormed, ILattice, IHashable
{
    Dot(a: Self, b: Self): Number;

    // Builds a value of this vector type from its components, in index order.
    // The receiver only selects the type; its own components are ignored.
    // Precondition: xs has exactly Count entries (for fixed-arity vectors).
    FromComponents(_: Self, xs: Array<Number>): Self;

    // Builds a value of this vector type with every component set to x (the
    // component-wise constant). The receiver supplies the arity, so unlike
    // FromComponents this is genuinely an INSTANCE member: VectorN.Broadcast reads
    // self's component count (numeric-structures.library.plato), and a
    // runtime-arity vector has no other source for it, so the receiver must be
    // `self: Self`, not the ignored-receiver form used by FromComponents.
    Broadcast(self: Self, x: Number): Self;
}
```
